## Canoeing and Wildlife by the River

After breakfast, the route begins with a photo safari along Araras Eco Lodge's private roads to the Clarinho River. On reaching the riverbank, guests board canoes and travel alongside the forest, watching for its wildlife.

Giant river otters inhabit this area. With luck, you may spot a family with young near the water. There is also an opportunity to try fishing for piranhas, followed by a barbecue lunch beneath the trees and time to relax in a hammock.

If Sentinela camp is inaccessible because of the weather, road conditions or the state of the area, the canoe excursion takes place on the Corixo River instead. In that case, guests return to the lodge for lunch after their time on the water. This is an included alternative route.

## Howler Monkey Tower and Night Safari

In the afternoon, a walk along the Howler Monkey Trail leads to a 25-metre observation tower. Watch the sunset here and take in sweeping views of the Pantanal.

After dinner, guests set out in a specially equipped vehicle in search of nocturnal wildlife. Sightings depend on natural conditions.

## Horseback Riding in the Pantanal

The morning route passes through open floodplains and shallow water. Pantaneiro horses are adapted to the region's wetlands and have long accompanied local people in their work and travels.

From horseback, you can watch the landscape shift between open ground, water and vegetation. After the ride, guests return to the lodge for lunch.

## The Rondon Trail and Jabiru Tower

In the afternoon, the group walks along the Rondon Trail to the 13-metre Jabiru observation tower. Under favourable conditions, a jabiru stork's nest may be visible from here, along with other birds.

The walk ends back at Araras Eco Lodge. Whether the nest and birds can be seen depends on natural conditions; the programme does not guarantee sightings.

## Discover Arequipa

Known as the "White City", Arequipa enchants visitors with its magnificent architecture built of *sillar*, a volcanic stone that gives the city its blend of colonial elegance and Andean charm. Surrounded by three imposing volcanoes — Misti, Chachani and Pichu Pichu — the city offers spectacular scenery that merges with its historic streets and squares. At Arequipa's heart lies the beautiful Plaza de Armas, where the grand cathedral and surrounding arches evoke the city's rich colonial heritage, while lively street scenes bring a contemporary touch. Walking through Arequipa's narrow streets feels like stepping into another era: around each corner are treasures such as the colourful Santa Catalina Monastery, a city within a city, rich in history and tranquillity.

The White City welcomes us on a tour beginning in the lovely colonial San Lazaro district, the site where Arequipa was founded. From here, we stroll along colourful geranium-lined streets before heading to the Carmen Alto viewpoint for magnificent views of agricultural terraces and the three volcanoes towering over the city: Misti, Chachani and Pichu Pichu. We continue to the colonial Yanahuara district, known for its Andalusian-style church and a viewpoint framed by beautiful stone arches.

## A Journey Through the White City's Colonial Landmarks and Volcanic Scenery

Next, we visit the impressive Santa Catalina Monastery, a religious complex closed to outsiders for almost 400 years. Its narrow streets, squares and gardens recall the old quarters of Seville or Granada. We then make our way to Plaza de Armas, where we can admire the cathedral and the arches surrounding the square. We also visit the Jesuit church, founded by the Jesuits in the 17th century, with its cloisters and celebrated San Ignacio dome.
